ranch: Rancho Sespe (also recorded as 'San Cayetano'), Ventura County, California
land_disambiguation: This target is the 8,881-acre Mexican land grant in the Santa Clara River Valley between Piru Creek (east) and Santa Paula Creek (west), including present-day Fillmore, Ventura County. Granted 1833 to Carlos Antonio Carrillo; U.S. patent to Thomas Wallace More 1872 (GLO map 397); the More brothers ran it as a cattle/agricultural ranch; later owned by Keith Spalding. NOT to be confused with: (a) the More family's Santa Barbara-area holdings (Rancho La Goleta / More Mesa); (b) the Sespe Creek/Sespe Gorge backcountry (Los Padres NF) which shares the name 'Sespe' but is upstream of the ranch lands; (c) 'Rancho Santa Margarita' in Orange County or the San Diego 'Santa Margarita y Las Flores'; (d) Piru / Rancho Temescal, immediately east across Piru Creek.

physical_only_collections: Museum of Ventura County — Research Library & Archives, 100 E. Main Street, Ventura, CA 93001; phone (805) 653-0323; https://venturamuseum.org/research-library-about/ . Holds 100,000+ image prints/negatives (daguerreotypes, cyanotypes, tintypes, albumen, glass-plate), 3,300 postcards, 2,300 slides covering the Mission/Rancho period to present; 40 Rancho Sespe items are online at photographs.venturamuseum.org but the great majority of holdings are on-site only. Rights on online items are undetermined ('personal or research use only') — contact library staff for rights determinations and higher-resolution/other uses.

Fillmore Historical Museum — Ynez Haase Library (research by appointment), 350 Main Street, Fillmore, CA 93015; https://www.fillmorehistoricalmuseum.org/ . The museum is housed partly in the relocated 1919 Rancho Sespe Bunkhouse and holds extensive vintage photographs, records, maps and crate labels of Rancho Sespe, Bardsdale, Sespe and Piru, including private family collections of people who lived/worked on the ranch. Founded 1972 by Edith Moore Jarrett. Online 'Crate Labels' and 'Rancho Sespe' pages exist but most photographic holdings are physical, viewable by appointment.

The Huntington Library — San Marino, CA; reference@huntington.org, (626) 405-2191. Holds the 'Sespe Rancho collection, 1829-1944' (412 items): E. M. Sheridan's manuscript history of Rancho Sespe, historian correspondence, interview notes (Howard F. Pressey, Keith Spalding), a small number of drawings and pictures, and copies of the 1854 California Land Commission legal documents filed by Carlos Antonio Carrillo. OAC finding aid: https://oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/c86d5zhq . Open to qualified researchers by prior application; finding aid is collection-level only (no item-level image list online). Huntington also contributes 1 (unidentified) Rancho Sespe item to Calisphere.
dead_ends: David Rumsey Historical Map Collection (davidrumsey.com) — query 'Sespe' returned 0 results (totalResults:0). No Rancho Sespe map located.

Library of Congress general search 'Rancho Sespe' — apart from the HABS Sespe Ranch Bunkhouse (ca2392), all other hits were 19th-c. newspapers (Daily Los Angeles Herald, etc. reporting the 1877 T. W. More murder), 1940s telephone directories, and USGS geology/water-supply bulletins of the Santa Clara Valley — no additional Rancho Sespe photographs or ranch maps.

USC Digital Library full-resolution asset for CHS-45750 ('View up the Sespe River, 1921') — item is Public Domain / CC BY and downloadable in principle, but the USC IIIF/asset host (iiif.library.usc.edu / digitallibrary.usc.edu asset 2A3BF1BK6FD) did not resolve (HTTP 000 / HTML redirect) in this environment; full-res file not retrieved.
LAPL 'David C. Cook's residence, Piru' — depicts Piru / Rancho Temescal (Del Valle land east of Piru Creek), NOT Rancho Sespe; excluded as different land.
Note on the More family: Thomas Wallace More and brothers also held Santa Barbara-area ranchos (e.g. Rancho La Goleta / More Mesa) — those images are DIFFERENT land and were not collected here.
